description.narrative: FKE launched a national report (February 2021) on the Informal economy (impact of COVID 19 included). The report consolidates the results from a desk review, a diagnostic of informal sector enterprises (Jua Kali enterprises) based on a quantitative survey covering a total sample of 1476 respondents from Greater Nairobi, Nakuru, Mombasa, Kisumu and Kakuma area and 429 respondents from Kakuma and Kalobeyei (to cover as well the particular situation of refugee entrepreneurs) and a rapid assessment of the impact of the COVID-19 crisis on the informal economy. The diagnostic study provides FKE with a better understanding of the characteristics, perceptions and needs of services of Jua Kali enterprises but also with an assessment of the level and types of organizations formed by informal entrepreneurs, the knowledge and perception of informal economy entrepreneurs of existing employers’ organizations and FKE in particular, including d interactions they have developed with these organizations. It also provides insights on the challenges that informal enterprises face to operate and/or upgrade their business, how they perceive the advantage /disadvantage of formalization of their business and what services they would like to receive in priority. The results provide a basis for FKE to define suitable services in order to membership to the informal economy. FKE presented a range of policy options on how to address issues in the post pandemic future (six briefings were held with members and two with Ministries). The ILO (with the support of the Government of the Netherlands) supported policy work in two areas, informal economy and digital platform, commissioning research in both. Concerning the informal economy, the ILO supported the design and implementation of the diagnostic of the situation in the informal economy units in selected cities and in refugee camps which included the definition of the method of diagnostic (mix of quantitative and qualitative methods), support the design of data collection tools (questionnaires for the quantitative study; guidelines for focus group discussions and qualitative interviews), follow-up of the implementation, analysis of results and review and finalization of the report, including recommendations.. The ILO ensure the full involvement of FKE at all stages in the process. FKE subsequently used this material for policy positions (2 policy frameworks were developed May and September 2021).

description.narrative: Federation of Kenyan Employers (FKE) adapted its organizational structure and processes in response to changes in the business environment posed by COVID 19. In July 2020, FKE developed a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) to make institutional capacities more efficient and effective in light of COVID 19. FKE conducted 18 interviews with senior staff and Board members along with 4 external focus group sessions with members. FKE introduced a new planning tracker tool that enabled it to accurately manage the implementation of BCP and adjust workplans every quarter. In January, FKE Board adopted the planning tracker tool and mainstreamed it across all FKE departments as a management tool. As part of the BCP process, FKE surveyed members 7 times (between March 2020 and July 2021). 421 survey responses formed the basis of the BCP and resulted in services being adapted along with new policy priorities. On services, FKE developed 5 guides and 2 videos on key aspects of managing the crisis. Following the BCP recommendations, FKE recalibrated its training offer by shifting it on-line, and achieved 45% higher attendance than in pre-COVID 19 times. Regular webinars became a new FKE service (24 webinars conducted in 2020-21). These online events widened accessibility to members (increase in 40% attendance at all types of events). On policy, FKE submitted policy proposals to government on measures to support business and stem job losses such as PAYE, VAT relief (May 2020/August 2020). FKE developed a policy guideline on the platform economy (September 2021) which saw big growth during the pandemic. These combined efforts, all emanating from the BCP to manage the pandemic, enabled FKE to increase overall revenue by 3% in August 2021 compared to 2020. The ILO established a survey platform and designed survey questionnaires that enabled FKE to run 7 member surveys to identify their needs and concerns as COVID 19 unfolded. Consequently, the ILO supported the development of a BCP which was specifically designed in terms of a contingency and continuity plan for FKE. The ILO developed a new ‘BCP tracker tool’ to support implementation. The ILO additionally provided FKE with two policy frameworks, one as the pandemic broke (March 2020) and the second in February 2021 to support economic recovery policies. The ILO provided FKE with a range of COVID 19 material that was specifically customized for FKE use into 5 guides (Workplace Guide on managing COVID 19; Return to Work Guide on managing covid-19; Work From Home Guide COVID; Retrenchment Guide COVID 19; how the Kenyan workplace is changing), 2 training videos (A BCM training video; work from home video), webinars and speeches. The ILO also supported FKE in building a policy and services agenda for the post pandemic environment. A national Survey (July 2021) was conducted (131 responses) and a report developed with ILO support. The BCP identified key areas were FKE needed capacity strengthened in order to deliver its recommendation. Subsequently the ILO supported 7 FKE staff members to successfully complete the following ITC training courses: E-learning course on Skills Anticipation and Matching (September 2020); sectoral approaches to skill development (November 2020); and Digitalization of services (May June 2020).
